function_description: Returns a sorted copy of an array.
update_description: The kind argument to jax.numpy.sort() and jax.numpy.argsort() is now removed. Use stable=True or stable=False instead.

function_description: Returns a reshaped copy of an array with the specified shape.
parameters: shape (DimSize | Shape) – integer or sequence of integers giving the new shape, which must match the size of the input array. If any single dimension is given size -1, it will be replaced with a value such that the output has the correct size.
order (str) – 'F' or 'C', specifies whether the reshape should apply column-major (fortran-style, "F") or row-major (C-style, "C") order; default is "C".
copy (bool | None) – unused by JAX; JAX always returns a copy, though under JIT the compiler may optimize such copies away.
note: Unlike numpy.reshape, jax.numpy.reshape will return a copy rather than a view of the input array. However, under JIT, the compiler will optimize-away such copies when possible, so this doesn’t have performance impacts in practice.
update_description: The newshape argument to jax.numpy.reshape() is being deprecated and will soon be removed. Use shape instead.

function_description: Returns True if the input is a scalar or a zero-dimensional array.

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: input object to check; any type is valid input

note: JAX considers zero-dimensional arrays as scalars, differing from NumPy's behavior. This ensures JIT-invariance by treating zero-dimensional arrays as scalars.
update_description: jax.numpy.isscalar() now returns True for any array-like object with zero dimensions. Previously, it only returned True for zero-dimensional array-like objects with a weak dtype.

function_description: Computes the rank of a matrix using the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), determining the number of singular values greater than a specified tolerance.
note: The rank calculation may be inaccurate for matrices with very small singular values or those that are numerically ill-conditioned. Consider adjusting the rtol parameter or using a more specialized rank computation method in such cases.
update_description: The tol argument of jax.numpy.linalg.matrix_rank() is being deprecated and will soon be removed. Use rtol instead.

function_description: Compute the (Moore-Penrose) pseudo-inverse of a matrix.
parameters: a (ArrayLike): array of shape (... M, N) containing matrices to pseudo-invert.
rtol (ArrayLike | None): float or array_like of shape a.shape[:-2]. Specifies the cutoff for small singular values. Default determined based on dtype.
hermitian (bool): if True, input is assumed Hermitian, uses efficient algorithm (default: False).
rcond (ArrayLike | DeprecatedArg | None): deprecated alias for rtol. Will result in DeprecationWarning if used.
note: jax.numpy.linalg.pinv differs from numpy.linalg.pinv in the default value of rcond: in NumPy, the default is 1e-15. In JAX, the default is 10 * max(num_rows, num_cols) * jnp.finfo(dtype).eps.
update_description: The rcond argument of jax.numpy.linalg.pinv() is being deprecated and will soon be removed. Use rtol instead.
